cc.name: Creative Commons
cc.groupNote: For books, writing, art, music, and other creative work

licenses.Title: CC0
licenses.Intro: Public domain dedication: no rights reserved
licenses.Description: You give up your copyright and related rights as far as the law allows, so anyone can use your work for any purpose without asking.
licenses.Credit Required: No. Credit is welcome but not required.
Others Can: Copy, share, and change your work
licenses.Example Use: Research datasets, facts, or other material you want to be as easy to reuse as possible.
licenses.Things to Know: CC0 is technically a public domain dedication, not a license. It is meant to be permanent, so think carefully before you apply it. It does not give up any trademark or patent rights you hold.

licenses.Title: CC BY
licenses.Intro: Share and adapt for any purpose, with credit
licenses.Description: People can share and adapt your work for any purpose, including commercially, as long as they credit you.
licenses.Credit Required: Yes. Others must name you, link to the license, and say if they made changes.
licenses.ShareAlike: Not required. Others can license their own contributions however they like.
Others Cannot: Imply that you endorse them or their use of your work
Add restrictions that block what the license allows
licenses.Example Use: Blog posts, photographs, teaching materials, or articles you want shared as widely as possible.
licenses.Things to Know: The most flexible of the licenses that require credit.

licenses.Title: CC BY-SA
licenses.Intro: Share and adapt with credit; adaptations use the same license
licenses.Description: People can share and adapt your work, even commercially, if they credit you and license their adaptations under the same terms.
licenses.Credit Required: Yes. Others must name you, link to the license, and say if they made changes.
licenses.ShareAlike: Required. Adaptations must use the same license or a compatible one.
Others Must: Share adaptations under the same license, or a compatible one
Others Cannot: Imply that you endorse them or their use of your work
Add restrictions that block what the license allows
licenses.Example Use: Collaborative projects, like wikis, where improvements should stay open to everyone.
licenses.Things to Know: Works in the spirit of copyleft software licenses. Because adaptations must stay under the same terms, it can be hard to combine with work under other licenses.

licenses.Title: CC BY-ND
licenses.Intro: Share unchanged, even commercially, with credit
licenses.Description: People can copy and share your work, even commercially, as long as they credit you and do not change it.
licenses.Credit Required: Yes. Others must name you and link to the license.
licenses.Adaptations: Not allowed. Others cannot share edited, remixed, or translated versions.
Others Can: Copy and share your work unchanged
Others Cannot: Share modified, remixed, or translated versions
Imply that you endorse them or their use of your work
Add restrictions that block what the license allows
licenses.Example Use: Reports, essays, or artwork that should be shared widely but kept exactly as you wrote or made them.
licenses.Things to Know: Others cannot translate or remix your work and share the result. Projects that accept only free-culture licenses, such as Wikimedia Commons, do not accept ND works.

licenses.Title: CC BY-NC
licenses.Intro: Share and adapt non-commercially, with credit
licenses.Description: People can share and adapt your work for non-commercial purposes as long as they credit you.
licenses.Credit Required: Yes. Others must name you, link to the license, and say if they made changes.
licenses.Commercial Use: Not allowed. Use must not be primarily aimed at commercial advantage or money.
Others Cannot: Imply that you endorse them or their use of your work
Add restrictions that block what the license allows
licenses.Example Use: Art, music, or photography you want people to remix and share but not sell.
licenses.Things to Know: What counts as "non-commercial" can be unclear, so consider adding a short note that explains what you mean. Projects that accept only free-culture licenses, such as Wikimedia Commons, do not accept NC works.

licenses.Title: CC BY-NC-SA
licenses.Intro: Non-commercial, with credit; adaptations use the same license
licenses.Description: People can share and adapt your work for non-commercial purposes if they credit you and license their adaptations under the same terms.
licenses.Credit Required: Yes. Others must name you, link to the license, and say if they made changes.
licenses.Commercial Use: Not allowed. Use must not be primarily aimed at commercial advantage or money.
licenses.ShareAlike: Required. Adaptations must use the same license or a compatible one.
Others Must: Share adaptations under the same license, or a compatible one
Others Cannot: Imply that you endorse them or their use of your work
Add restrictions that block what the license allows
licenses.Example Use: Course materials or creative projects that others can build on, as long as the new work stays non-commercial and under the same terms.
licenses.Things to Know: What counts as "non-commercial" can be unclear, so consider adding a short note that explains what you mean. Projects that accept only free-culture licenses, such as Wikimedia Commons, do not accept NC works.

licenses.Title: CC BY-NC-ND
licenses.Intro: Share unchanged and non-commercially, with credit
licenses.Description: People can copy and share your work, unchanged, for non-commercial purposes as long as they credit you. This is the most restrictive of the six main CC licenses.
licenses.Credit Required: Yes. Others must name you and link to the license.
licenses.Commercial Use: Not allowed. Use must not be primarily aimed at commercial advantage or money.
licenses.Adaptations: Not allowed. Others cannot share edited, remixed, or translated versions.
Others Can: Copy and share your work unchanged
Others Cannot: Share modified, remixed, or translated versions
Imply that you endorse them or their use of your work
Add restrictions that block what the license allows
licenses.Example Use: A portfolio, essay, or report you are happy to have shared for free, but not sold or edited.
licenses.Things to Know: What counts as "non-commercial" can be unclear, so consider adding a short note that explains what you mean. Projects that accept only free-culture licenses, such as Wikimedia Commons, do not accept NC or ND works.

licenses.Title: Unlicense
licenses.Intro: Public domain dedication with no conditions
licenses.Description: Dedicates your software to the public domain with no conditions, so anyone can use, change, and sell it without asking or giving credit.
licenses.Credit and Notices: No. Nothing needs to be kept or credited.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes. Others can include it in closed-source products.
licenses.Patent Grant: Not mentioned. The license says nothing about patents.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Code under the Unlicense can be included in practically any other project.
licenses.Things to Know: Public domain dedications work differently from country to country, so some organizations prefer a license such as MIT, BSD, or ISC. The software is provided without warranty.

licenses.Title: MIT
licenses.Intro: Short and simple; only requires keeping the notice
licenses.Description: A short, simple license that lets people do almost anything with your software as long as they keep your copyright and license notice.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. The copyright notice and license text must stay with copies of the software.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes. Others can include it in closed-source products.
licenses.Patent Grant: Not mentioned. The license says nothing about patents.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Code under this license can be included in projects under GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL, AGPL, MPL, and Apache-2.0, as long as its notice is kept.
licenses.Things to Know: One of the most widely used licenses. The software is provided without warranty, and you are not liable for damages.

licenses.Title: ISC
licenses.Intro: Like MIT, with even simpler wording
licenses.Description: A short permissive license that works much like MIT, with simpler wording. Others can do almost anything with your software if they keep your notice.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. The copyright notice and license text must stay with copies of the software.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes. Others can include it in closed-source products.
licenses.Patent Grant: Not mentioned. The license says nothing about patents.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Code under this license can be included in projects under GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL, AGPL, MPL, and Apache-2.0, as long as its notice is kept.
licenses.Things to Know: Often chosen for its brevity. The software is provided without warranty.

licenses.Title: BSD 2-Clause
licenses.Intro: Permissive; keep the notice in source and binaries
licenses.Description: A permissive license that requires keeping your copyright notice and license text, in both source and binary distributions.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Source copies keep the notice. Binary copies must reproduce it in documentation or other materials.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes. Others can include it in closed-source products.
licenses.Patent Grant: Not mentioned. The license says nothing about patents.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Code under this license can be included in projects under GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL, AGPL, MPL, and Apache-2.0, as long as its notice is kept.
licenses.Things to Know: Similar to MIT, with a slightly different notice requirement for binary copies. The software is provided without warranty.

licenses.Title: BSD 3-Clause
licenses.Intro: Like BSD 2-Clause, plus no endorsement with your name
licenses.Description: A permissive license like BSD 2-Clause with one more rule: others cannot use your name or your contributors' names to endorse or promote products built from your software without written permission.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Source copies keep the notice. Binary copies must reproduce it in documentation or other materials.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes. Others can include it in closed-source products.
licenses.Patent Grant: Not mentioned. The license says nothing about patents.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Code under this license can be included in projects under GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL, AGPL, MPL, and Apache-2.0, as long as its notice is kept.
licenses.Things to Know: The extra no-endorsement clause is the main difference from BSD 2-Clause. The software is provided without warranty.

licenses.Title: Apache 2.0
licenses.Intro: Permissive, with an explicit patent grant
licenses.Description: A permissive license with an explicit patent grant from contributors. Others can use it in open or closed products if they keep notices and state their changes.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Keep the license, copyright notices, and any NOTICE file, and state significant changes.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes. Others can include it in closed-source products.
licenses.Patent Grant: Yes. Contributors grant patent rights. Those rights end for anyone who sues claiming the software infringes a patent.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Code under Apache-2.0 can be included in GPL-3.0, LGPL-3.0, and AGPL-3.0 projects. The FSF considers it incompatible with GPL-2.0-only.
licenses.Things to Know: Longer than MIT or BSD. It does not grant trademark rights, and the software is provided without warranty.

licenses.Title: MPL 2.0
licenses.Intro: Share changes to your files; the rest can stay closed
licenses.Description: A copyleft license that applies to individual files. Changes to MPL-covered files must be shared under the MPL when distributed, but they can be combined with files under other licenses in a larger work.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Keep license and copyright notices.
licenses.Sharing Requirements: Yes, per file. Modified MPL files must be shared in source form under the MPL when distributed.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes, with limits. Files you add can stay closed, but changes to MPL files must be shared.
licenses.Patent Grant: Yes. Contributors grant patent rights for their contributions.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: By default it can be combined with GPL, LGPL, and AGPL code through the MPL's secondary license provision, unless a file is marked as incompatible with secondary licenses.
licenses.Things to Know: A middle ground between permissive licenses and the GPL family. The software is provided without warranty.

licenses.Title: LGPL 3.0
licenses.Intro: Share changes to the library; programs that use it can stay closed
licenses.Full Name: GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0
licenses.Description: A copyleft license designed for libraries. Changes to the library must be shared under the LGPL (or GPL) when distributed, but programs that only link to it can use other licenses, as long as users can replace the library with a modified version.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Keep license and copyright notices, and state changes.
licenses.Sharing Requirements: Yes, for the library. Programs that only use it are not required to share their own code.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: Yes, if the product links to the library and meets the LGPL conditions, such as letting users swap in a modified library.
licenses.Network Use: No special rule. Running it as an online service does not trigger any sharing duty.
licenses.Compatibility: Can be combined with GPL-3.0 code. Programs that link to an LGPL library can use other licenses if the LGPL conditions are met.
licenses.Used By: Qt offers it as one of its licensing options
licenses.Things to Know: Some fine print applies to how a closed-source program may link to the library, so read the conditions before relying on it. As with the GPL, you can choose "only" or "or later" wording.

licenses.Title: GPL 2.0
licenses.Description: A strong copyleft license. Anyone who distributes your software, or a work based on it, must offer the source under GPL v2.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Keep license and copyright notices, and state changes.
licenses.Sharing Requirements: Yes. When distributed, the whole combined work must be offered with source under the same license.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: No, not in distributed products. A distributed product that includes your code must be released under the same license, with source.
licenses.Patent Grant: No express grant. Version 3 added one.
licenses.Network Use: No. Running it as an online service does not count as distribution.
licenses.Compatibility: Not compatible with Apache-2.0 code or with GPL-3.0-only code. Code marked "GPL-2.0-or-later" can be combined with GPL-3.0.
licenses.Used By: Linux kernel (GPL-2.0-only), WordPress (GPL v2 or later)
licenses.Things to Know: You can choose "only" or "or later" wording, and the choice affects compatibility with GPL v3 code.

licenses.Title: GPL 3.0
licenses.Intro: Strong copyleft, with a patent grant
licenses.Description: A strong copyleft license. Distributed copies and works based on your software must be offered with source under GPL v3, and contributors grant patent rights.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Keep license and copyright notices, and state changes.
licenses.Sharing Requirements: Yes. When distributed, the whole combined work must be offered with source under the same license.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: No, not in distributed products. A distributed product that includes your code must be released under the same license, with source.
licenses.Network Use: No. Running it as an online service does not count as distribution.
licenses.Compatibility: Compatible with Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, ISC, and LGPL-3.0 code, and can be combined with AGPL-3.0 code. Not compatible with GPL-2.0-only code.
licenses.Used By: GIMP and Ansible (GPL v3 or later)
licenses.Things to Know: Version 3 adds patent terms and rules about hardware that blocks modified software from running. You can choose "only" or "or later" wording.

licenses.Title: AGPL 3.0
licenses.Intro: Strong copyleft that also covers network use
licenses.Full Name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
licenses.Description: Like GPL v3, but it also covers software used over a network. People who run a modified version for users online must offer those users the source.
licenses.Credit and Notices: Yes. Keep license and copyright notices, and state changes.
licenses.Sharing Requirements: Yes. When distributed, or offered over a network, the whole combined work must be shared with source under the same license.
licenses.Closed-Source Use: No. A product that includes your code and is distributed or run as an online service must be released under the same license, with source.
licenses.Network Use: Yes. Users who interact with a modified version over a network must be able to get its source.
licenses.Compatibility: Can be combined with GPL-3.0 code. The combined work is then subject to the AGPL's network clause.
licenses.Things to Know: Some organizations avoid AGPL software, so choosing it can limit adoption by businesses.
